name: Ellen Sturgis Hooper
bio: Ellen Sturgis Hooper (1812–1848) was a Boston poet, a friend of Margaret Fuller and a member of the circle around the Transcendentalist journal The Dial. She married Robert William Hooper, a physician, and was the mother of Marian 'Clover' Hooper, later the wife of Henry Adams.
She published very little in her lifetime; her best-known lines, a six-line poem on beauty and duty, appeared unsigned and untitled in the first number of The Dial in July 1840.

poems.title: Beauty and Duty
poems.author: Ellen Sturgis Hooper
poems.text:
I slept, and dreamed that life was Beauty;
I woke, and found that life was Duty.
Was thy dream then a shadowy lie?
Toil on, sad heart, courageously,
And thou shalt find thy dream to be
A noonday light and truth to thee.
